annotations.text:
Drill-down, not accordions

Tap a row, get a page. The row shows its current value so the list still answers "what is my goal, which theme" without opening anything.

On a detail page:
  · back arrow top-left, 44px target
  · the page title replaces "Settings"
  · the bottom nav is GONE

Dropping the nav is deliberate — with one way out, back is unmissable, and the page gets its full height. Tapping a tab mid-edit would also lose the edit silently.

Account and Appearance are wired here; the other rows are drawn but inert.

Account page carries everything about the person: avatar, name, member-since, the email marked read-only as the sign-in identity, then password and sign out, then delete.

Delete account is last and separate. It is also the thing the privacy policy already promises but the app cannot yet do — designing it here is the first half of keeping that promise.

Four states, not two. "Unsaved changes" is the one usually missing, and it is the one that prevents the loss — otherwise you only learn the form was dirty by leaving it.

The button never changes width or position between states.

Two ways in, one record

New accounts accept at sign-up: a real checkbox, never pre-ticked, sitting directly above the button that acts on it. Create account stays disabled until it is ticked — a visible gate beats an error message after the fact.

Existing accounts get the sheet on next open. Their own screen shows through behind it, dimmed: this is someone with data here, and the sheet should read as one step in front of their app rather than a wall that lost it.

No dismiss, no "remind me later" — consent that can be swiped away is not recorded consent. Sign out stays, because that is the honest way to decline.

Both need a column recording WHICH version was accepted and when, or you cannot prove anything later and cannot re-prompt when the terms change.
